# Installing rizin and rz-frida

The plugin is a rizin core plugin: it registers the `frida` command group
inside rizin. It needs rizin v0.9.0 or later (the per-core plugin context
from [rizin#6404](https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin/pull/6404)). CI builds
against v0.9.1. It also needs rizin's development files. With
`-Dfrida_core=enabled` and no manual paths, meson fetches the frida-core
devkit for the host (see `frida_version` in `meson_options.txt`). Without
frida-core the plugin still builds, and device commands answer with a
`frida_unavailable` error.

The examples below use a prefix of `$PREFIX`. Replace it with wherever you
install rizin (`/usr/local`, `$HOME/.local`, and so on). `rizin -H` prints
the paths of the rizin you are running (`RZ_PREFIX`, `RZ_INCDIR`,
`RZ_LIBDIR`, `RZ_LIB_PLUGINS`) if you are not sure.

## Install via rz-pm (experimental)

If you already have rizin and meson:

```bash
$ rz-pm install rz-frida
```

rizin development files (pkg-config or cmake) must be present,
and on Windows the command must run inside a Visual Studio developer
prompt.

## 1. Build rizin from source

```bash
$ cd ~/rizin
$ meson setup build --prefix=$PREFIX --buildtype=release -Duse_gpl=true
$ ninja -C build && ninja -C build install
$ export PATH="$PREFIX/bin:$PATH"
```

The plugin build finds rizin through pkg-config:

```bash
$ export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$PREFIX/lib/$(uname -m)-linux-gnu/pkgconfig
```

On some layouts the pkg-config directory is `$PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig`. Use
whichever contains `rz_core.pc`.

## 2. Build the plugin

From the plugin source tree, with rizin on `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`:

```bash
$ meson setup build-frida --prefix=$PREFIX -Dfrida_core=enabled
$ ninja -C build-frida && ninja -C build-frida install
```

Meson tries pkg-config `frida-core-1.0` first, then fetches the matching
devkit (see `frida_version` in `meson_options.txt`) into
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rz-frida` or `~/.cache/rz-frida` on Linux, and
`~/Library/Caches/rz-frida` on macOS. To pin a local devkit instead:

```bash
$ meson setup build-frida --prefix=$PREFIX \
    -Dfrida_core=enabled \
    -Dfrida_include_dir=/path/to/frida-core-devkit \
    -Dfrida_library=/path/to/frida-core-devkit/libfrida-core.a
```

The gadget and `frida-server` you put on a device should match the
frida-core version this plugin was built against (`meson configure
build-frida | grep frida_version`).

## 3. Verify

```bash
$ rizin -N -q -c 'fridasj' malloc://8
{"ok":true,"result":{"active":false,"state":"closed"}}
```

The command group exists, the plugin is loaded:

```bash
$ rizin -N -q -c 'frida?' malloc://8
```

![Plugin loaded](img/intro/plugin-loaded.png)

![Command group help](img/intro/frida-help.png)

> **Note:** a session-requiring command without a session answers with
> `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"invalid_target","message":"no session is open"}}`.
> That is expected: the plugin is loaded, the session is not.

## 4. Run the test suite

```bash
$ meson test -C build-frida -j1 -t 6
```

The tests cover the URI parser, session lifecycle, protocol helpers, the
agent message protocol, the null backend, command registration and the
agent script protocol. They run without any device.

## Platform notes

| Platform | Notes |
|---|---|
| Linux | the instructions above |
| macOS | the devkit links Foundation, CoreFoundation and AppKit |
| Windows | build inside a Visual Studio developer prompt |
| musl / bionic | link the static devkit. Android cross builds are in the release workflow |

## Rebuilding after changes

```bash
$ ninja -C build-frida && meson install -C build-frida
```

If ninja says there is nothing to do but the sources changed, `touch` the
changed files first. After an agent script change, the build regenerates
the embedded agent header.

> **Note:** stale plugin copies shadow a fresh build. If commands
> disappear after a rebuild, remove extra `librz_frida.so` files under
> `~/.local/share/rizin/plugins/` and keep the copy under `$PREFIX`.
